The text of IEC standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventions are, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. 3.2 3.2.1

Manufacturing

stages

and

sub-contracting of an approved manufacturer in a

Manufacturing stages in a factory non-IEC member country a)

Circuits manufactured by an approved manufacturer in a factory of his company in a non-IEC member country can be delivered under the system only if the conditions of IEC Publication QC 001002, Sub-clause 10.3, are met.

b)

The sectional specification shall indicate if, for technical reasons the principle of extension of manufacturer's approval shall only, not be applied for a given sub-family or type of circuit.

3.2.2

Sub-contracting

of manufacturing

processes

Circuits that are partly manufactured in a factory other than the approved manufacturer's can be delivered under the system only when the conditions of IEC QC 001002, Sub-clauses 10.3 and 11.1.2, are met.

The sub-contracted processes one or two of the following: trimming of elements; mounting of components; encapsulation.

To cover the different requirements of various electronics market three assessment levels (K,L,M) are specified for approval as sectors, described in the sectional specification. Assessment level M is the assessment level L is higher with larger minimum mandatory level; requiring sample sizes and assessment level K is the highest level, even larger sizes and also specifying screening tests.

qualifying circuits (CQCs) are tested in given to a manufacturing facility on the rules, processes and quality control in Clause 3.6 and the relevant sectional

in addition to the testing of With capability approval, the manufacturer specifies in a capability manual circuits, materials and processes and his procedures for design, accepts monitoring of these by the National Supervising exercised by the Inspectorate (NSI). Control is combination of the lot-by-lot tests on all circuits released, qualifying together with periodic tests on capability with tests on circuits (CQCs) -and, if applicable, together on a routine process vehicles, to validate the capability basis.

After any specified period of recovery, the post-test end-point measurements shall be a repetition of the pre-exposure measurement, prescribed in Sub-clause 4.5.14.3.1. Measurements may be made whilst the circuit is within the chamber or after removal at the manufacturer's discretion.
